headline: South Asia: Pakistan Army destroys Afghan Taliban posts in response to firing at Angoor Adda: state media
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistan Army destroys Afghan Taliban posts in response to firing at Angoor Adda: state media.
- Western Russia: 3 Killed as Ukraine Renews Drone Strikes Against Oil Refineries.
- Persian Gulf Region: ‘Need a Plan B’: Yemenis in Aden prepare for another war as missiles fall.

Full breakdown follows.

United States - bottom line: Record deployment for destroyer USS Spruance casts doubt over US Navy maintenance.
- Military Times, 22 hours ago: Record deployment for destroyer USS Spruance casts doubt over US Navy maintenance.
The Arleigh-Burke class destroyer USS Spruance has set a post-World War II record for a U.S. Navy destroyer deployment and is raising questions about the maintenance work that could follow its eventual return.

The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak confirmed that Ukrainian drones targeted three oil refineries and one gas chemical complex overnight.

Russian strike drones attacked Shostka in Sumy Oblast, killing a 43-year-old woman and injuring eight people, one in a serious condition, the mayor says.

General Alexus Grynkewich has said that third-party transfers of Patriot missiles are moving forward, with work underway on future PURL defence packages.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Russia strikes Kharkiv shopping centre with jet-powered drone, forcing temporary closure.
A Russian Shahed-type UAV has hit the roof of the Dafi shopping centre in Kharkiv, forcing the facility to temporarily suspend its operations.

- Balkan Insight, 10 hours ago: Democracy Digest: Was Orban’s Name Floated for UN Chief as a ‘Stalking Horse’.

- Balkan Insight, 10 hours ago: Moldova Steps Up Border Security Amid ‘Unprecedented’ Threats.
Border police chief Ruslan Galusca says the threat to Moldova’s borders from drones, drug trafficking and illegal migration has grown massively since Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of neighbouring Ukraine.
- Balkan Insight, one hour ago: Tragedy that Led to Change: Serbia Marks Two Years Since Canopy Collapse.
As Serbia remembers the 16 people killed when a concrete canopy at the Novi Sad railway station collapsed, students who toppled the ruling party two years later say they can look to the future with hope.
- Balkan Insight, 4 hours ago: New Exhibition Features Italian Photojournalist’s Work from Wartime Sarajevo.
An exhibition of Italian photojournalist Mario Boccia’s work from wartime Sarajevo opens at the History Museum of Bosnia and Herzegovina on November 2. The exhibition shows Sarajevans’ daily life in a dark time.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan Army destroys Afghan Taliban posts in response to firing at Angoor Adda: state media.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Pakistan Army destroys Afghan Taliban posts in response to firing at Angoor Adda: state media.
Pakistan’s armed forces targeted and destroyed several Afghan Taliban posts and military positions in areas adjacent to South Waziristan and Parachinar, state media reported on Friday, citing security sources. According to state-run Radio Pakistan, the army “gave a befitting reply to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban along the Pak-Afghan border in the Angoor Adda area” on Tuesday. “Using heavy weaponry, the Pakistan Army forced Afghan Taliban personnel to abandon their posts and flee,” the report said.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, 7 hours ago: Rubio hosts G20 ministers as Iran, Ukraine wars divide members.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will host his G20 counterparts, including Russia’s Sergei Lavrov, for talks on Friday that are expected to be fractious, with wars in Ukraine and Iran and surging energy prices fanning discord. The foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta, Georgia, taking place just days before crucial US midterm elections, will set the stage for a December G20 leaders’ summit in Miami at President Donald Trump’s Doral resort.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 10 hours ago: Cop martyred in KP's Bajaur as terrorists attack police post: official.
BAJAUR: A police officer was martyred after terrorists attacked a police post in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bajaur district, officials said on Friday. The attack on the police post in Silai Pati area in the remote Barang tehsil, bordering Malakand district, occurred late on Thursday night. Mansoor Khan, a spokesperson for the district police, while confirming the attack, told Dawn that a group of Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists targeted the Silai Pati police post, prompting the personnel to retaliate bravely and courageously.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Crypto exchange Binance freezes assets after $6.3bn 'complex' security breach.
Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Friday it was working to resolve a “complex attack” that hit around $6.3 billion in funds, with about half that amount frozen to prevent a massive theft. The company — the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes — said investigations had “uncovered additional points of breach”, contrary to initial findings that suggested the hack involved a single compromised laptop. “This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it,” Binance wrote on X.

- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Georgia parents' $37m verdict cut to $2m, appeals court raises it to $3m.
A couple in Georgia has triumphed in their legal battle, securing a $3 million judgment after an appeals court re-evaluated their son's death case. This decision overturned a previous reduction of a $37 million jury award to just $2 million. Their son, who succumbed to stage-four Burkitt lymphoma, faced complications during his treatment. The court recognized the parents as distinct entities under state law, enabling them to seek higher restitution.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Patrick Stewart's $3.9M Brooklyn sale revealed after death at 86.
Star Trek and X-Men star Patrick Stewart quietly sold his Brooklyn apartment for $3.9 million in July 2025, more than a decade after purchasing it for $2.5 million. The actor made a $1.4 million gain on the sale. The transaction has come into focus following his death at 86, highlighting his connection to Park Slope.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Two friends turn $15 Denver haunted house into 18 Halloween attractions.
Two friends, Chris Stafford and Warren Conard, opened a haunted house in a Denver shopping complex in 2002, charging $15 per ticket. What began as a side business has grown into a multimillion-dollar company with 18 seasonal Halloween attractions across the US. The company paid around 4,500 workers during the 2025 Halloween season and is now expanding into Christmas entertainment.
